title: ready-01b: split heca into server and client, still in one process
summary: AppState splits into server state (sessions, terminals, agents) and client state (window, drawing, docks, overlays); standalone keeps working unchanged.
description:
First step of the server/client model (F012 accepted decisions "heca runs standalone or as a server…" and "Two windows on one session…"). Depends on P098 (library). Nothing changes for the user: standalone is the server part and one client part inside one process, talking through one clear interface.

## Current state
- `heca/src/app_state.rs` (1326 lines) holds, side by side: the window and GPU renderers (heca_renderer Grid/Text/Primitive/Image/Blur/Compositor), retained chrome trees (`chrome_tree` ~816, `panes` ~826, `terminal_layers` ~707), and the state: `session: Session` (~722), `backends: BackendStore` (~724), `chrome_state: SharedChromeState` (~866). 81 files use AppState; ~65 places touch the window.
- Terminal data is already separate from drawing: `heca-core/src/backend/snapshot.rs` — TerminalSnapshot (:194, screen as data) and TerminalDamage (:40, which rows changed). The snapshot carries pixel cell sizes (cell_w/cell_h), which belong to the client.
- `SharedChromeState` already mirrors the state the sidebars read — the natural start for what the server sends.

## Goal
- Server part: sessions (a list, even if only one for now), workspaces/columns/panes, terminal backends, runtime/agent state, notifications store.
- Client part: window, renderers, retained chrome, docks, overlays, per-window view (shown workspace, focused pane, scroll, open overlays).
- One interface between them: the client sends actions and input; the server sends state changes and terminal snapshots + changed rows. The client builds all UI from that data — the server never sends interface.
- Every action sorted: changes state → server; window only (open palette, scroll the view, show a dock) → client.
- Pixel cell sizes move to the client; rows x cols come from the client.

## Preserve
- Standalone behaves exactly as today; all tests green; AGENTS.md § 0 (DOM-shaped events, a component owns its input, no fixes at the call site).

## Done when
- The app runs through the interface with server and client in one process; a test drives the server part with no window at all.
notes:
**Handoff context update:**
Step 1 (ServerState carve-out incl. backends/notifications/git cache/programs), 2a (notifications via plain-data ServerAction -> Vec<Change>), 2a-2 (store owns no signal; window owns AppState::toasts) and 2c (git cache private, ServerState::refresh_git) are built and committed locally on feat/p104-notifications-server (HEAD 10dd94bf); not pushed. Step 3 decided: option A (accepted decision 2c249a29).

**Remaining work:**
PR 1: move the view (active_ws, workspace_switch, viewport, scale, per-workspace ViewOffset) out of Session/ScrollingSpace into a client WindowView, standalone behaviour identical. PR 2: layout-op ServerAction interface. Then facts (PaneFacts/Server::facts/Change::FactsChanged), 2b terminals (parked until stream 1's refactor A and 5a merge), 2d action SIDE descriptor field + routing.

tasks.title: Split AppState into a server part and a client part behind one interface, in one process
tasks.description:
Execution task for P104 — read the phase and F012's accepted decisions first. Current: `heca/src/app_state.rs` (1341 lines, ~100 fields) mixes renderers/window/retained chrome with `session`, `backends`, `chrome_state`; 91 files name AppState. `heca-core/src/backend/snapshot.rs` already gives terminal data (TerminalSnapshot) and changed rows (TerminalDamage). Edge cases: actions that touch both sides; per-window state now implicit in AppState (focus, scroll, open layers); tests that build AppState (it needs a window today — the server part must not).

## Measured (origin/main, 2026-10-01)
- Only 4 handler files touch window fields directly (9 refs); the 140 WmAction handlers are almost all state-only already. 271 refs to session/backends/terminals in 43 files.
- `terminals` (T449) is already the CLIENT's view of a terminal (chrome::terminal::Terminal is a widget); the server side of a terminal is `BackendStore` (app/backend_store.rs).

## Field map (decided with the orchestrator 2026-10-01)
SERVER (shared by every window): session (content part: workspaces, columns, panes, layout options), backends, notifications store (queue, lifecycle, timers), git_runtime_cache, programs config, pane runtime facts (PaneFacts), action registry handlers + the catalog (actions run where state is).
CLIENT (per window): window, surface/device/queue/renderers (primitive, text, image, grid, compositor, blur, backdrop, background), terminal_layers + scratch, theme/appearance/font_config/zoom/cell sizes/scale_factor, retained chrome (chrome_tree, panes, columns, layers, overlays, window_root, chrome_host, context_menu_registry, action_shortcuts), terminals + terminal_presses, mouse/modifiers/selection, input_mode + prefix state, focused_pane/last_focused/last_visited, expose cursors, hint letters, pending menus/drops, widget_keymap, notification_hovered/pick_open signals, searches (a window's own view of a pane search), needs_redraw, window_focused, current_cursor.
MIXED — each needs a decision:
1. Session: shared content vs per-window view (active_workspace_idx, workspace_switch animation, viewport_size, scale, and the scrolling view offset inside each workspace's ScrollingSpace). Design decision for Antonio (options written to the orchestrator); NOT guessed.
2. SharedChromeState: sidebar content mirror (workspaces container state) = sent by the server; region sizes/visible, focus, cursors, keyboard targets = client.
3. NotificationRuntime: the store (server) vs the toast projection/hover/pick signals (client). Split in step 2.
4. action_catalog: one catalog; the client reads descriptors.
5. search_store/history and `confirm` config: per-user, decide when the interface exists.

## Steps (agreed)
1. ServerState carve-out, behaviour-neutral, one PR: new heca/src/server/ module; ServerState holds notifications store, git_runtime_cache, programs, pane runtime facts; AppState owns `server: ServerState`; mechanical path change; compiler lists every window touch of server state = the work list for step 2. WITHOUT `backends` (stream 1's process PR reshapes backend_store.rs/terminal_process.rs; backends joins ServerState in a small follow-up commit once that PR merges). Leave `terminals` on the client.
2. The one interface (client sends actions/input; server returns state changes + terminal snapshots/changed rows); a test drives the server part with no window; split notification store from its projection.
3. Session view split — options to the orchestrator, who takes the decision to Antonio.

---
**Completion summary:**
T525 complete: AppState split into server (shared content — sessions, layout, backends, notifications) and client (per-window view). C9 shown-workspace by id; C12 focused-pane per window by id; C10 floating geometry + is_active + focus_domain per window; C5 terminal snapshot/damage read through ServerState::terminal_view; C7 docs/server-client-architecture.md. Committed 606431e4 on feat/t525-server-client-split (rebased on current main). heca-core + heca tests green (0 failures), clippy clean, reviewed. Not yet PR'd to main.

checklist.title: Map every AppState field to server or client; agree the interface
Server part: sessions list, layout, backends, runtime/agent state, notifications
Client part: window, renderers, retained chrome, docks, overlays, per-window view
Sort every action: server (changes state) or client (window only)
Terminal: snapshot + changed rows through the interface; pixel cell sizes client-side, rows x cols from the client
Standalone runs through the interface unchanged; a windowless test drives the server part
PR 2 (layout door): a content change from one window must shift every window's view offsets — the door returns a plain view-shift each window applies
PR 2: the shown workspace becomes a workspace id, not an index (a shared workspace removal leaves another window's index stale)

PR 2 (layout door): geometry and animation cached in the shared content use the last window's size and clock — column widths, pane sizes, floating positions (Workspace::update_working_area rescales them), column/pane move animations, and the drag offset interactive_move_offset (per-window visual state). Also per-window focus kept in the content: focus_domain and a floating pane's is_active

2c: per-window visual state still living in the shared content: the slide animations of swap and place (heca-core layout/handle/swap.rs slide_from, used by moves.rs) join the other animations to move out of the content
Move each column's active pane (Column.active_pane_idx) out of the shared content into the window's view: the focused pane is per window (decision 463ccd07), but it still lives in the session today.

When rebasing onto stream1's stack: keep Session::set_options in heca-core and drop stream1's startup::apply_layout_options (both fix the same reload bug: workspaces kept an old copy of the layout settings). Keep stream1's heca_config::loader::config_from_layers.

B2.2 (NEXT) — the server moves panes and columns between workspaces, takes and places panes, swaps across columns and workspaces, and floats, without touching any window's view; each window shows the change itself. Then the server loses its access to a window's view (ServerLayout::workspace_mut) and the old view-bound moves are deleted. (Moves inside one workspace already work this way: PR #284.)
2b — terminals live behind the server: a window asks the server for a terminal's rows instead of owning the terminal (empties AWAITING_TERMINALS).
